sourceAreas.rationale: API, configuration and HTTP lifecycle. Includes request and error handling, readiness probes, configuration loading, example inputs and the published API.
Authentication. Covers principal mapping, TLS checks, explicit revocation and the documented identity contract.
Operation policy and approvals. Covers object and request grants, approval evidence, semantic policy, dispatch and audit coordination.

Custody registry, schema, and operator validation. Schema and example custody data express admissible claims. The capability projection is generated validation input, never independent hardware evidence.
Cryptographic operation boundaries. Includes bounded execution, signature and certificate support, context-bound wrap and authenticated envelope handling.
Cosmos wire policy and integration fixtures. Covers the supported SDK subset, runnable software and opt-in devnet/hardware validation, and documented evidence boundaries.
Durable policy and offline control-plane state. Includes export inspection/readback, local state and collector-backed rollback detection. The drill is evidence tooling.

Hardware providers and token access. Includes PKCS#11, PIV, standalone OpenPGP, reauthorization, PC/SC and credentials. The local PIN import design remains subject to its separate custody and physical acceptance gates.
Client adapters. Includes both separate Go modules, their CLIs and RPC carrier, examples, and the draft-only OpenBao contract.
Audit recorder, collector, and shipping units. Covers local events, collector/server and trail adapters, service timers and credentials, authenticated continuity and operational state observations.
Metrics and monitoring contracts. Includes metrics exposition, separate KMS and node alert rules, and monitoring deployment prerequisites.

Daemon and operational admission. Includes daemon lifecycle, preflight, active-passive CLI and admission, session publication and reservation components. Baremetal peer startup, image and restore semantics are covered by the other owner's shard.

Build dependency and CI policy controls. Includes build and scan workflows, dependency pins, inventory tooling, bench scripts and evidence classification. Tool and dependency files contribute to software verification scope only.

Scenario harness and shared deployment evidence plumbing. Accounts explicitly for scenario drivers, proof assertions, software TPM and boot fixtures, sample evidence, matrix runners and hardware-only commands. Shared baremetal scenarios validate those product contracts without moving their runtime ownership.

Non-product assertion code and fixture data in assigned runtime modules. Explicit evidence-only disposition for checked-in tests, testdata, mutation ledger renderer and test integration modules. Individual assertions backing requirements are cited separately.
Evidence-only disposition for cited standalone assertions and adjacent workflow, custody, qualification and alerting checks. These files help verify product and harness behavior.

knownGaps.description: Normal single-node service startup can lack an independently established history floor. The frozen daemon opens file-backed policy state, and an optional etcd observer does not prove existing backend/WAL continuity or gate operation admission. The first-store and restore startup contract is a proposed change with unresolved authority and same-artifact start proofs.
knownGaps.releaseGate: Required for normal single-node continuation and safe lost-disk restore acceptance.
